structured_output.summary: C042 in src/sim/car.ts: groundUnderBody no longer does `bodyTs.length = 0` / `bodyHs.length = 0` followed by `push`, which let V8 free and reallocate each array's backing store on every call. It now writes by index with a local count (`bodyTs[n++] = -half; = 0; = half;`, then `bodyTs[n++] = lip` / `foot` in the same order as before), fills `bodyHs[i]` for i < n with the same groundAt call, and stores the count in a new module scratch `let bodyN` next to bodyTs/bodyHs. visualPose loops `i < bodyN` / `j < bodyN` instead of using `.length` (in both the airborne branch and the hull search). The arrays keep their largest size, so in steady state no array is allocated. The same floats are computed in the same order, so replays and bot laps don't change. I updated the doc comments to match (only the first bodyN entries are current). New test tests/sim/car-pose-scratch.test.ts runs 6 bots on Dust Bowl (which has ramps) and wraps Array.prototype.push while carView is called for every car each tick. It expects 0 pushes: this failed with 4680 on the old length=0+push code and passes after the fix. A second check confirms that a car's view doesn't depend on which car was viewed before it, so stale scratch entries past bodyN are never read. pnpm typecheck and pnpm test (105 files, 718 tests) pass. I couldn't rerun the judge's allocation probe in this sandbox, so the per-frame byte drop is not yet measured.
